Locally, docker-compose exposes Postgres itself on 5432 with no pooler, so the problems below only show up after deploy. The pool is sized at 20 server connections per service, and long transactions starve checkout, so keep transactions short and never hold one open across an HTTP call to the ledger. The pooler runs in transaction mode: session state does not survive between transactions (no SET session variables, no advisory locks across transactions, no LISTEN/NOTIFY), and server-side prepared statements fail with 'prepared statement does not exist'. I added `src/db.py`:

```python
def get_conn():
    # Deployed environments connect through a transaction-mode pooler (port 6432),
    # where server-side prepared statements break, so turn them off.
    return psycopg.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"], prepare_threshold=None)
```

I haven't run anything against a database to test it.

- **`prepare_threshold=None` matters.** A team note says production and staging reach Postgres through a pooler on port 6432. That pooler doesn't support the prepared statements psycopg 3 creates automatically, so without this setting queries fail with "prepared statement does not exist". It won't show up locally, because docker-compose connects to Postgres directly on 5432.

- **New dependency.** `psycopg` wasn't listed anywhere, so I added `psycopg>=3.1` to `dependencies` in `pyproject.toml`.

Because of the pooler, keep transactions short and don't hold one open across an HTTP call to the ledger. Session settings, advisory locks and LISTEN/NOTIFY also don't carry over from one transaction to the next.
